relevance_note: Autopsy case report of a woman with Alexander disease despite non-diagnostic GFAP sequencing: "this patient had pathologically confirmed AxD".
method_note: Read in full by hand; a small Python script in scratch only assembled the JSON and checked spans. The Markdown prints '>' as '>'; spans keep '>', values use '>'. Scope: the index patient (AxD diagnosis, GFAP c.469G>A called likely benign; kept because the authors do not dismiss it as non-causal and discuss it as possibly not entirely benign); affected relatives (mother, maternal grandfather, maternal uncle, brother; the brother had normal whole-exome sequencing, so no variant row); two previously published people with an individual-level fact: the Zhong et al case (ref 2, adult-onset AxD, D157N; linked to ref (2) through the reference list) and the 14-year-old Flint patient (intronic alteration). Left out: the asymptomatic, untested living sister and niece (neither tested nor affected); the Mork case (ref 1, only a title); families from ref 13 (no individual facts). The Zhong case's 'second variant of uncertain significance' has no printed description or gene, so no row. Hedged 'possible dysphagia' of mother/grandfather/uncle not recorded as observed; their checklist dysphagia left not reported. 'Problems walking' for the three relatives comes from 'They all had ...' (group naming them), marked inferred from group statement. Ataxia for the index patient left not reported: she had 'balance problems', and Friedreich ataxia was investigated, and the pedigree caption mentions ataxia in the family, but ataxia is not stated for her. Cerebral white matter abnormality left not reported: autopsy dysmyelination is in white matter tracts from amygdala to pons and spinal cord, not described as cerebral white matter; recorded as a free feature. Kim et al's biophysical prediction for D157N was not demonstrated experimentally, so functional evidence is not reported. gnomAD's 'benign to likely benign' is a database view, not used as the authors' classification. General laboratory work-up 'within the normal range' recorded as written as one excluded row; it excludes nothing more specific. Age at last evaluation for the index patient is her age at death (62); age at presentation was 58; onset age not stated (3-year history at presentation). Publication year is not printed in the document. No contradictions found.
